key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: Reversing the South Carolina Supreme Court, the Court held that ICWA § 1912(f) does not apply where the parent never had custody, that § 1912(d)'s active-efforts requirement applies only where termination would precipitate the breakup of an Indian family, and that § 1915(a) preferences do not bar a non-Indian adoption when no preferred party has come forward.
key_cases.relevance: This is the controlling ICWA authority for South Carolina courts — it arose from a South Carolina adoption and narrows when active efforts, the heightened §1912(f) showing, and §1915(a) placement preferences are triggered at intake.
key_cases.quote: Consistent with the statutory text, we hold that §1912(d) applies only in cases where an Indian family's "breakup" would be precipitated by the termination of the parent's rights.

key_cases.holding: The South Carolina Supreme Court affirmed the family court's denial of the adoption and transfer of custody to the Cherokee biological father, holding ICWA §§ 1912(d) and 1912(f) barred termination — a holding REVERSED by the United States Supreme Court in Adoptive Couple v. Baby Girl, 570 U.S. 637 (2013).
key_cases.relevance: This is South Carolina's only substantive ICWA decision and shows how its courts analyze tribal notice, 'parent' status and transfer at intake, but its §1912(d)/(f) holdings were reversed and must not be cited as current law.
key_cases.quote: We affirm the decision of the family court denying the adoption and awarding custody to the biological father.

mandatory_reporters: Listed professionals only, acting in their professional capacity (South Carolina is not a universal-reporter state) — S.C. Code Ann. § 63-7-310(A)
Physicians, nurses, dentists, optometrists, medical examiners, coroners, and employees of a county medical examiner's or coroner's office
Any other medical, emergency medical services, mental health, or allied health professional
Members of the clergy, including Christian Science practitioners and religious healers
Clerical or nonclerical religious counselors who charge for services
School teachers, counselors, principals, assistant principals, and school attendance officers
Childcare workers in a childcare center or foster care facility
Undertakers, funeral home directors, and employees of a funeral home
Volunteer non-attorney guardians ad litem serving on behalf of the South Carolina Guardian ad Litem Program or Richland County CASA
Any other person may report and is encouraged to report — S.C. Code Ann. § 63-7-310(D)

other: Encourages, condones, or approves the commission of delinquent acts by the child and those acts are shown to be the result of the encouragement, condonation, or approval
